points.description: States that a doubly-linked list allows insertion and deletion operations to be done in constant time (O(1)) / efficiently, without traversal (main advantage).

levels.says: Says insertion/deletion is faster or more efficient but does not mention constant time or O(1).

points.description: States that this applies to operations at or before a given location/node (e.g. deleting or inserting before a given node), which a basic singly linked list cannot do in constant time because it needs traversal from the head to find the predecessor.

levels.says: Mentions only that it is easier to move backwards/has a previous pointer, without linking it to insertion/deletion before a location.

points.description: States that this includes operations at the end of the list (e.g. deleting the last node) in constant time (given a tail pointer), or explains the reason: each node has both next and previous pointers.

rubric.notes: Full marks need constant-time insertion/deletion, including before a given location, and the end of the list or the previous-pointer reason. Part marks for vague efficiency claims or only backward traversal. Do not credit only 'uses more memory' or unrelated claims.
